brief_summary: Mechanism diagram: two horizontal timelines showing radio wake-event frequency. The 2.4GHz dongle timeline shows dense, evenly spaced wake ticks; the Bluetooth timeline shows sparse ticks with an amber bracket over one gap, illustrating why Bluetooth Low Energy's longer sleep between connection intervals produces longer battery life than a 2.4GHz dongle's higher-frequency polling.
data_sources: wireless-keyboard-buying-guide.mdx § 'Battery life is a duty-cycle question, not a marketing one' — 'Bluetooth Low Energy is built to let the radio go quiet between the negotiated connection intervals and wake only to check in or send an event'

wireless-keyboard-buying-guide.mdx § 'Battery life is a duty-cycle question, not a marketing one' — 'a 2.4GHz dongle link... is built to keep that polling rate high and consistent, which means the radio wakes far more often regardless of whether a key was actually pressed'
